subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Terroir in Coffee
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Terroir in Coffee.

hook.text: Wine lovers talk about terroir. Coffee has it too—soil, climate, and altitude shape every cup.

buildup.text: Volcanic soil in Guatemala adds mineral brightness. Red clay in Kenya gives bold, juicy acidity.

discovery.text: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe beans taste of jasmine and citrus—a fingerprint of that specific microclimate.

twist.text: Plant the same variety in a different country and the flavor changes dramatically. Place matters.

climax.text: Single-origin coffee lets drinkers taste terroir directly—one farm, one harvest, one unique flavor.

punchline.text: Every cup carries a postcard from where it grew.

quiz.question: What is terroir in coffee?
options: How soil, climate, and altitude shape flavor

details.summary: Like wine, coffee expresses terroir: the unique combination of soil, climate, altitude, and geography that gives a region's coffee its distinctive character. Ethiopian Yirgacheffe tastes different from Colombian Huila because of their distinct growing environments.
details.whyItMatters: Terroir is why single-origin coffees command premium prices. Recognizing terroir deepens appreciation for coffee as an agricultural product shaped by place.
takeaways: Terroir combines soil, climate, altitude, and local conditions
It explains why the same variety tastes different by region
Single-origin coffees showcase terroir at its purest

faq.question: What factors make up coffee terroir?
faq.answer: Soil type and mineral content, altitude, rainfall patterns, temperature variation between day and night, shade from surrounding vegetation, and even neighboring crops all contribute. Volcanic soils in regions like Guatemala add distinct mineral qualities.

faq.question: Can you taste terroir in a cup of coffee?
faq.answer: Trained tasters can identify major growing regions by flavor. Ethiopian coffees often show floral and berry notes, Kenyan coffees have bright tomato-like acidity, and Sumatran coffees are earthy and full-bodied. These are terroir signatures.
